nopSolutions/nopCommerce:7841.title: Quotes. PDF export
nopSolutions/nopCommerce:7841.body:
**Description:**
The official [Quotes](https://github.com/nopSolutions/nopCommerce/issues/279) plugin works very well and provides a solid foundation for creating and managing quotes.

However, it seems the plugin was not designed for easy sharing of quotes outside the system (which I believe is an important aspect in e-commerce).
In our company, we often face situations where:

- Customers request a PDF version of the quote.
- Administrators want to send a quote directly to an email address, without having to select a registered customer, since we sell through multiple channels, and sometimes the customer requesting the quote has not yet registered in the system (allowing us to bring potential customers into the system through this quote).

We assume that other companies using NopCommerce might encounter similar requirements.

**Requested Improvements:**

- PDF Export: Ability to export a quote as PDF including items, prices, total, customer info, date, logo, ...

**Benefit:**

- Supports collaboration and approval workflows.
- Enables flexible sales channels and easier sharing with customers or internal departments.
- Reduces manual effort of copying quote details into external documents or emails.

nopSolutions/nopCommerce:8257.title: [FromHeader] and [FromBody] string action parameters always bind to null
nopSolutions/nopCommerce:8257.body:
A `string` action parameter with `[FromHeader]` or `[FromBody]` always comes back `null`, even when the header/body is present in the request. `[FromQuery]` and `[FromRoute]` are fine, and non-string header parameters are fine too - it only affects `string`.

Minimal repro on any controller:

```csharp
[HttpGet("test")]
public IActionResult Test([FromHeader(Name = "X-Test")] string value) => Content(value ?? "null");
```

`curl -H "X-Test: hello" .../test` returns `null`; a plain ASP.NET Core project returns `hello`.

The cause is `NopModelBinderProvider`: it's inserted ahead of the built-in header/body binder providers and returns `StringModelBinder` for every `string` regardless of `BindingInfo.BindingSource`. `StringModelBinder` only reads the value providers (query/form/route), so header/body strings never bind.

Version: 4.90.6, .NET 9.

nopSolutions/nopCommerce:8436.title: PunchOut: outgoing cart XML contains an empty UnitOfMeasure
nopSolutions/nopCommerce:8436.body:
**nopCommerce version:** 5.00
**Plugin**: PunchOut cXML Integration (Misc.PunchOut)

**Impact**
Suggested improvement.

**Description**

The PunchOutOrderMessage generated when submitting a cart for approval contains an empty UnitOfMeasure element in the item details.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Send a valid POST /punchout/setup request.
2. Open the Start Page URL returned in the response.
3. Add a product to the shopping cart.
4. Click Submit for Approval.
5. Capture the browser POST at the receiving endpoint.
6. Decode the cXML-urlencoded form field and inspect the item’s ItemDetail element. 
7. Observe that UnitOfMeasure is empty

**Expected behaviour / suggested improvement**

Each item should contain a valid unit-of-measure code appropriate to the product and supported by the receiving procurement system.  

It isn't clear where this value should be sourced from.   Ideally, this would come from a configurable product or SKU selling-unit mapping which currently does not exist.   An optional store default (such as `EA`) would be beneficial.

nopSolutions/nopCommerce:7907.title: Allow to rename custom wishlist names
nopSolutions/nopCommerce:7907.body:
### **Description:**

In the Multiple Wishlist feature, users can create and delete custom wishlists, but there is **no option to edit or rename** an existing wishlist. This results in poor usability — for example, if a user enters the wrong name, they are forced to delete the wishlist and recreate it instead of simply correcting the name. This behavior breaks the expected CRUD flow and causes confusion.

---

### **Steps to Reproduce:**

1. Login as a registered customer
2. Go to **My Account → Wishlists**
3. Click **“Create New Wishlist”** and enter any name
4. Attempt to edit or rename the wishlist

---

### **Expected Result:**

User should be able to edit/rename a custom wishlist name through an **Edit** / **Rename** option in the UI.

---

### **Actual Result:**

There is **no option available to rename** a custom wishlist. Only **Create** and **Delete** actions are provided.

---

### **Impact:**

* Reduces usability and flexibility
* Forces unnecessary deletion and re-creation
* Inconsistent behavior compared to standard wishlist CRUD logic (Create, Read, Update, Delete)


### **Attachment:**
https://jam.dev/c/53217b4b-6c08-4314-a6fe-762d404c322f

ShareX/ShareX:578.title: Only install signed updates
ShareX/ShareX:578.body:
The update functionality in ShareX is currently insecure. It will download whatever's on github right now and execute it. Instead, the developer of ShareX should keep a private key that the updates are signed with. The client will check if the update is signed before executing it. The developer should keep in mind secure storage best practices in relation to the private key.

This issue is made in light of the puu.sh compromise where a malicious update was pushed out, as they perform no code signing.

ShareX/ShareX:8639.title: Add “Print” functionality back to the new Image Editor
ShareX/ShareX:8639.body:
In the previous ShareX Image Editor, there was a built‑in Print option (Image → Print / Ctrl+P) that allowed users to quickly send screenshots directly to a printer.
In the new Image Editor UI, this functionality appears to be missing:

The Print menu entry is no longer available
Ctrl+P is now mapped to “Pin image” instead of printing

This creates friction in workflows where users need to:

Quickly print screenshots (e.g. QA, manufacturing, support, logistics)
Avoid saving + opening another application just to print

Currently, the only workaround is:

Save or copy the image
Open it in another app (Paint, Photos, etc.)
Print from there

This adds unnecessary steps compared to the old editor.

ShareX/ShareX:7355.title: Suggestion: Pin to screen (from file) as a context menu option
ShareX/ShareX:7355.body:
I had a good look around and couldn't find this option in the application or suggested here, so here it is (sorry if I still missed it somewhere). Also thank you @Jaex and everyone else for contributing to this great piece of software.

I often use the **_Edit with ShareX_** option in the context menu that shows when right clicking an image file. It would be great to also have a **_Pin to screen with ShareX_** option, something like this:

![25-03-2024_21-29-05](https://github.com/ShareX/ShareX/assets/81528115/a05384b7-767a-4d1d-9a8c-8ef74d679b30)

This option would basically skip the following steps: 
**_Tools > Pin to screen... > Pin to screen from file... > Navigating to the image we would like to pin in the Open File dialog_**
(Yes, the first three steps could be eliminated by using a **_Pin to screen (From file)_** hotkey, but the Open File dialog would always remain).

By having a **_Pin to screen_** option in the context menu, we would have a direct reference to the image that we want to pin, so this would eliminate the need for going through the Open File dialog, and the already existing logic of pinning an image to the screen from a file could then be executed.
